changes.reason: Restored the condition that half revenue applies when a firm already filled the order this turn under Deregulation.
Added the complete eligible-ship storm rules and per-ship roll results requested in the question.
Numbered each answer field as requested.

answers.answer: 1. “Simultaneously roll one die for each held office card. Add one per fatigue on that card; Chairman also adds one. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire.” 2. “Move retiree to Pensioners, flip card into Vacant Offices, return its fatigue to supply.” Commanders have no office card and do not roll normal office attrition.
answers.evidence: London Season—Attrition: quoted operative roll and disposition.

answers.answer: 1. Only players who retired at least one pensioner select: each must take or discard one display card, in descending actual total retirement spending. Ties go to most total windows, including new prizes, then clockwise from PM; the acting player may peek at display blackmails. 2. Do not replace chosen or discarded cards during selection. If the display empties, immediately skip every remaining eligible player. Then discard all remaining cards and refill exactly three—prestige faceup and blackmail facedown—even if nobody took a card. Return all remaining Pensioners to their supplies.
answers.evidence: London Season—Prestige and Retirements: complete selection order, display and pensioner disposition.

answers.answer: 1. At phase start, check where the opportunity marker was; take a main action once, or you may take it twice if the marker already matched it. Then place or move the marker onto the chosen main action. Only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action afterward; that extra action is never doubled by the marker and never moves it. 2. “With at least four vacant offices, place one additional writer once this turn, so a doubled Writer action can place three total.” Thus with four vacant offices and the marker already on Enlist Writer, the doubled action can place two writers plus the one-time extra writer, three total.
answers.evidence: Family phase steps 1–4; Enlist Writer row; direct operative facts quoted.

answers.answer: 1. After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one. Repeat while both remain. Pieces in Court are Company shares. With no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order. Seeking a share never pays family cash into Company treasuries; purchase money is paid to the bank when the applicant is placed in a Stock Exchange queue space.
answers.evidence: Family—Seek Share row and New Company shares paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. Fill vacant offices in ascending number on their card backs. The designated hirer chooses a candidate and moves that member into the office; its owner gets the card. When promoting an officeholder, transfer its fatigue to the new card and insert its old card, vacant, into ascending hiring order. If no candidate exists, or the hirer is vacant, skip the office; it stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring. For an ordinary own-family hire, verbal consent is required from every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool. Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt from Nepotism consent.
answers.evidence: Hiring procedure and Nepotism table, including exceptions.

answers.answer: 1. The former Chairman first announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority, meaning more than half of current shares. Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one winner’s Company shares into the Chairman slot and give the title marker. It still counts as a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms. If no candidate gets support, the former Chairman picks any shareholder, including self, without Nepotism consent. If the Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns, placing a member from supply or, if necessary and possible, a prize (losing that prize’s VP); if impossible, there is no Chairman.
answers.evidence: Chairman election paragraph; both ordinary and deadlock fallback rules quoted.

answers.answer: 1. First commit resources and cash: all cash for a Company-office check comes from that acting office’s treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, then roll; use the lowest die. A 1–2 succeeds; a 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources and office-specific limits allow; a 5–6 is catastrophic failure, ends that office’s actions, returns its officeholder to supply, discards fatigue and flips the card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander and firm procedures modify this. Do not take a dead action with no effect or chance of success, such as trade with no ship or deploy without dice merely to trigger possible officer losses.
answers.evidence: Company Operation—Success checks: full operative sequence and limits.

answers.answer: 1. The Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, each adding £5 to Balance. Each additional advance requires consent of players controlling a majority of Company shares, with the Chairman counting; never pass the Debt track end. Then allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries, lowering Balance by each transfer. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved while respecting the total borrowing rules. Cash already in offices remains there for their use.
answers.evidence: Actions—Chairman: borrowing and allocation procedure.

answers.answer: 1. The Manager of Shipping must spend treasury until £2 or less remains. Lease an extra ship for £2; fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without owner consent; buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Place each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China once its office exists. Extra ships serve only until Refresh.
answers.evidence: Actions—Manager of Shipping: full expenditure list and destinations.

answers.answer: 1. Declare regions for Trade including the home region, and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from the President’s treasury buys one die; subtract one per declared nonhome region. A successful Trade can fill one order per ship in that Presidency’s sea zone; ships are not exhausted. Fill as many orders as possible in the declared regions: the first writer goes to the home port, and every later order must extend the connected route filled during this same Presidency’s Trade. Writers from another Presidency cannot extend that route, but writer count does not limit capacity: use all available writers, then continue with filled-order tokens for remaining ships, and those tokens continue this Trade’s route. A President may not fill another President’s home region even if that office is vacant. Increase Balance by each order’s printed value, or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn under Deregulation. The President receives £1 from the bank per order and writer owners receive £1 per writer placed. At most one successful Trade per President per turn; failed attempts and retries stay within that President’s uninterrupted opportunity.
answers.evidence: Presidency operations and Trade: declaration, check, route, capacity, rewards and limit.

answers.answer: 1. A Commander may deploy to their Presidency’s home, any associated region, or any region bordering an associated region; they cannot target another home region or another Presidency’s Company-controlled region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order to give the action an effect. Exhaust chosen officers and regiments for one die each and local alliances for their printed dice, then subtract the combined strength of the target and all other regions in its empire, counting the target only once; Company-controlled defense strength is zero. Roll the normal check, and a noncatastrophic failure may be retried with remaining resources. After each attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns an officer to supply. Regiments never roll officer-loss checks.
answers.evidence: Actions—Commanders and Deploy, steps 1–3.

answers.answer: 1. On success, take loot from the bank equal to £4 per target tower plus the faceup loot modifier, with a minimum of surviving officers used in this attempt plus one for the Commander. Count only surviving participating officers from this attempt and the regiments and alliances used this attempt. Repeat the payout cycle until the loot is distributed: pay the Commander’s family first £1 for the Commander and £1 for each of their used surviving officers; then other families clockwise £1 per used surviving officer; then the bank £1 per used regiment and per used local-alliance piece regardless of strength. The Commander receives one trophy per target tower. After loot and trophies, remove the target tower and dome (and every matching empire flag throughout India if it was a capital), open all target orders and remove all target unrest; on new conquest place the loot/control token region-symbol side up above the associated President’s box, Governor overlay in the conquered region, and only the Governor card in Vacant Offices awaiting Hiring. If Elephant faced outward from the conquered region, move it fully inside. On catastrophe, the Commander returns half their family’s trophies rounded up and the Commander member to supply; exhausted officers still check losses, and there is no office card to vacate.
answers.evidence: Actions—Deploy successful payout/control tables and catastrophe paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. Take the printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces that pool by one regardless of result. On success, take £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, then choose exactly one option: build one ship stage, commission one regiment into the Army associated with the Governor’s President, or add an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President’s treasury. For building, if no partial ship is in the Governor’s region, that success places the partial ship there; if one is already there, that success completes it into the sea zone associated with the Governor’s President. A commissioned regiment has officer-like strength, loot paid to bank, and no officer-loss rolls. Each Tax after the first this turn adds regional unrest. Any unsuccessful roll adds one unrest in the region; catastrophe also removes the officeholder under the normal rule. Repeat with the shrinking pool until choosing to stop, no dice remain, or catastrophe.
answers.evidence: Actions—Governors: Administer procedure and option table.

answers.answer: 1. If Balance cannot cover Company expenses, take £5 emergency loans. Each loan advances Debt by one only while a track space remains; at maximum Debt keep taking loans without advancing Debt further. Newly added emergency Debt causes no extra expense this turn. After using emergency loans set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower Standing two. Then compare remaining Balance with the expectations under current Standing and lower Standing one if Balance is lower. Finally the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends; each costs one cash per Company share and pays each owner £1 per share, including the Chairman. If total cash paid as dividends is strictly greater than expectations, advance Standing one space.
answers.evidence: Revenue—Company expenses, expectations, dividends: full ordered procedure.

answers.answer: 1. An Invasion or Rebellion against a Company region triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve the primary Crisis first, then secondary regions in Bombay → Madras → Bengal Army order; within each Presidency, its Commander chooses the order of associated regions. Primary normal Crisis strength is normal Invasion/Rebellion strength plus unrest in the target; every secondary Rebellion uses only the unrest cubes in that secondary region, with no event modifier or empire strength. For defense, the occupied associated Commander chooses and exhausts pieces, with normal trophy gains/losses. If Commander is vacant, Military Affairs acts in the Commander’s stead and gains/loses no trophies; if both are vacant, Chairman chooses and gains/loses no trophies. This is defense, not appointing a Commander. Exhaust active Army pieces equal to Crisis strength, or as many as possible; local alliance strength is usable once and cannot be split among purposes. If newly exhausted pieces equal Crisis strength, the attack fails and defense succeeds: remove all unrest in the attacked region; actual Commander gains one trophy (substitute gains/loses none), and if it defeated a normal primary Invasion also remove one attacker tower if possible. If strength does not equal, the attack succeeds and defense fails, causing Region Loss. The summary explicitly leaves unresolved how indivisible excess alliance strength counts, including strength 2 versus a strength 1 attack.
answers.evidence: Events—Attacks on Company, Mounting defense table and unresolved counting boundary.

answers.answer: 1. At resolution, support −1 or less fails: discard the law, resolve a dilemma’s If Failed text, and the Opposition Leader returns the token and takes the PM dial; the new PM moves the proposed policy one space either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. Support zero or higher passes: place the law with passed laws, PM takes the passed-law token, resolve the selected policy and then immediate law effects. Finally restore every voting card to regular orientation after either result. If law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring. Before voting, PM moves the dial’s arm clockwise or counterclockwise and stops on the first policy space matching the chosen law’s bottom icon; that space fixes target and consequence.
answers.evidence: Parliament—policy selection and Resolution paragraphs.

answers.answer: 1. In 1758 and Long 1710, at the very start of the turn before London Season, the PM may call the special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. It uses ordinary voting procedure and support threshold; no policy accompanies it, and the PM may vote against it. On a pass, lower Debt one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, give PM a passed-law token, and activate firms. On a failure, increase Company-share scoring value by flipping/placing the Court VP token, up to a maximum of ±3 VP per share; PM remains in power and the Deregulation law is not discarded. 1813 begins deregulated.
answers.evidence: Deregulation table and scenario note.

answers.answer: 1. After Family share creation and before Hiring, investments occur in any order until nobody wants more; the firm’s manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm, and PM resolves conflicts between firms. To form a firm, only someone currently managing none may do so: return one eligible Company share to supply or flip a workshop to its invested side; flip the family board to firm-charter side, place a family member as first firm share, set value cube at the leftmost track space, and take £5 from the bank into London treasury. To invest, with manager’s consent contribute a Company share or workshop in the same way, create one firm share and take £5 from bank to London. A firm may have up to ten shares; further investments still contribute £5 but create no shares. The Chairman share cannot be used; no Company share can be used when Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space; shares created this turn cannot be invested even if traded away. Invested workshops never return to uninvested and give neither bonus nor Company-failure VP, even if firm fails.
answers.evidence: Deregulation—firm treasuries and Firms phase investments.

answers.answer: 1. Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn; only a firm with at least one ship may select a trade strategy, and it may select a closed home port. Managers secretly and simultaneously select strategy and, for a trade zone/home port, commit a secret bid from London; the chosen home port must be open when filled, and selection does not open it. Reveal bids simultaneously but keep strategies facedown until the matching Presidency begins. Before its actions, matching firms reveal and roll one die per committed £1, paying the bid to bank; at least one 1 or 2 permits trade. Initiative is ship count minus successful dice (1s/2s), possibly negative. President’s successful Trade sets initiative the same way using Presidency ships. Fill in lowest initiative order; President chooses tied order and Company does not automatically go first. If President is vacant or never successfully trades, firms fill after Commander/Governors had their chance, with Chairman choosing ties. Fill only open orders, up to ships + 1, starting from strategy home port and tracing its own filled route. A firm may fill a given order only once per turn, not its own earlier order; it may refill another firm’s or Company’s order, and Company may refill firm orders. A previously filled order pays half listed revenue rounded down. Trade revenue goes to India treasury; advance Value one space per full £6 added there this turn.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies and competing trade: full timing, checks, initiative and fill rules.

answers.answer: 1. At Revenue before Company, firms act in initiative order then other firms; ties go to manager with most windows, then PM clockwise order. Expenses are £1 per charter ship plus the higher of share count or firm Value, payable from either or both firm treasuries. If unable to pay, dissolve unless rescued: shares go to Debtor’s Prison at −1 VP each, ships return to shipyards, charter flips to family side, workshops remain invested. Emergency investments follow normal Company-share/workshop rules; even if the ten-share cap prevents further shares, they pay expenses, any remaining cash is lost, and Value lowers one space per emergency investment. Or use an emergency negotiated merger with only one other firm: normal merger procedure including consent of every involved shareholder applies, and the other firm must first pay its own expenses if not already paid, then cover the endangered firm’s unpaid expenses. After expenses, manager may pay dividends from India treasury only. Each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to manager. Waiving requires both shareholder choice and manager consent; a shareholder may forgo any number of shares on any dividend. Record total actual cash paid out, not per-share dividend, on Company Balance track. Active non-Hobnob firm paying none records zero; Hobnob keeps its prior marker. Sweep remaining India money to London.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends procedures.

answers.answer: 1. Components are limited; when a supply runs out, complete as much as possible. Cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. All information, including discards and family cash, is public except facedown blackmail and temporarily concealed firm strategies/bids during selection.
answers.evidence: Components—Limits paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. Negotiable items are enterprises, facedown blackmail, family treasury cash, Company or firm shares, and promise cards. Officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail, PM dial and Chairman piece may not be traded. To transfer a share, return the old owner’s family member and replace it at the share’s location with a member from the receiving family. Blackmail may be shown privately but must stay facedown when traded; played faceup blackmail cannot be traded.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Negotiation table and share/blackmail transfer rules.

answers.answer: 1. An immediate transfer is binding. A promise of future behavior is nonbinding, except the guaranteed effect of a printed promise card can be called if possible. Promise-card calls follow their timing and limits, and no promise calls are allowed during Final Scoring. If simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, the guarantor chooses which to fulfill. A promise card may be transferred to a third party or back to its guarantor. Transferred resources cannot activate twice; for example, a workshop paid during Bonuses does not pay again after being sold during that phase.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Agreement/promise table and repeated activation example.

answers.answer: 1. Use the chosen scenario’s player setup cards; add three extra cards for five players or six for six players, shuffle and deal evenly. Place every listed holding: take cash from the bank and enterprise cards into each player’s area; place each office’s family member in that office and give its matching office card to that owner; put Company-share members in Court of Directors; place writers, officers and trainees in their indicated Presidency, Army or Training boxes; put a Commander in that Army’s Commander slot without an office card; take each shipyard and place its matching ship in the listed sea zone or on its shipyard if unfitted. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Separately, shuffle prestige and blackmail together into one deck, then deal three for the London Season display with prestige faceup and blackmail facedown.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–4: player cards, holdings, luxury VP and display.

answers.answer: 1. The game ends after the scenario’s final turn or when Standing reaches failure; normally failure is immediate. If failure occurs during Events in India, finish that phase before Final Scoring. If legislation causes failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring. Once the game is over, stop negotiations, calling promises and playing blackmail unless a card explicitly permits final-scoring use. During all of Final Scoring, no negotiations or promise calls are allowed.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: game end, phase completion and post-game limits.

answers.answer: 1. Power counts enterprises and Company shares at their current Power-track rates (bottom two positions count zero), plus one per passed-law token and trophy, two for PM, and printed card power including faceup or facedown blackmail and applicable spouse. Most/second awards are 3/1 VP on final turns 1–3, 5/2 on turns 4–6, and 8/4 on turns 7–8. A tied first group receives only the lower award each, with no other award; tied second receive none. Highest final VP wins. Ties go to most windows, then clockwise from PM.
answers.evidence: Scoring—Power award and Highest final VP paragraphs.

answers.answer: 1. If Company survives, add Court’s current VP value per Company share; if it failed, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop. Scores may be negative. After ordinary scoring, a surviving Company rolls office attrition and retires Pensioners with no prestige/display cards; if Company failed, draw one random Company failure card and resolve its printed consequence. If deregulated, firm shares are scored first, then each eligible shareholder may take one special retirement from supply before ordinary final scoring, whether Company survived or failed; the failure card does not replace that retirement.
answers.evidence: Final Scoring order, Court/workshops, and Final retirements/failure table.

answers.answer: 1. Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot be transferred. Make required enterprise/share trades immediately upon taking the spouse. Retirement discounts can stack and are personal; each discount is usable once per London Season and once during Final Scoring. Discounts reduce actual spending and therefore prestige-display priority. The summary does not list individual spouse restrictions or other card-specific effects; those are read from the relevant component.
answers.evidence: London Season—spouse and discount rules; Overview says spouse card-specific powers/restrictions are read from components.

answers.answer: 1. Whether a shipyard is returned because of Violet Effingham or an unpaid tax, its fitted ship stays in play. That shipyard cannot be purchased while its matching ship remains in play; purchase becomes possible after the ship returns.
answers.evidence: London Season—Returned shipyard rule.

answers.answer: 1. Enlist Writer places a family member in any Presidency’s Writers box; with at least four vacant offices it places one additional writer once this turn, so a doubled action can place three total. Enlist Officer places a member in Officers-in-Training. Purchase Luxury costs £4 to the bank and gains a luxury worth 2 VP while owned plus its window icon; it is a social enterprise. Purchase Shipyard costs £2 to the bank, takes the shipyard and places its matching ship unfitted on that shipyard; it is a shipping enterprise worth one vote and a £1 bonus while fitted. Purchase Workshop costs £5 to the bank and gains a manufacturing enterprise worth two votes and a £1 bonus; it is worth 1 VP if Company fails unless invested. Seek Share puts a member on an empty Stock Exchange queue space and pays the bank its listed £2, £3, £3, £4 or £5 cost; it is an applicant, not yet a share.
answers.evidence: Family action table, including cost, effect, vote/income and failure scoring facts.

answers.answer: 1. If placing a family piece and none are in supply, take one from any of your prizes and lose that prize’s printed VP; this also applies to firm-share creation. If no Family action is possible, take none and return the opportunity marker to supply.
answers.evidence: Family phase: forced piece reuse and no-action rules.

answers.answer: 1. If Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns, placing a member from supply or, if necessary and possible, a member from a prize and losing that prize’s VP. If this is impossible, there is no Chairman.
answers.evidence: Chairman election: empty Court exception and placement options.

answers.answer: 1. The Chairman chooses Director of Trade from current officeholders other than Chairman or Governor; if all offices are vacant, choose any writer. Commanders are not officeholders. The Chairman chooses Manager of Shipping from any writer. For Military Affairs, the Chairman chooses a Presidential Commander; if none, any officer; if none, any Officer-in-Training. The Director chooses a President from a writer of that Presidency or a Governor associated with it. The associated President chooses a Governor from a writer or officer in the region; a Commander is not an officer and is ineligible, and the member goes on the Governor overlay. The Chairman chooses any writer for China, which is hired immediately upon creation. Governor General replaces Director of Trade and is hired the same way. For ordinary own-family hires, verbal consent is required from every other player represented in the candidate pool; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. If no candidate exists or the hirer is vacant, skip the office, which remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
answers.evidence: Hiring table, Nepotism rules and vacancy skip procedure.

answers.answer: 1. The Director may make repeated Special Envoy checks, paying £1 from the Director’s treasury per die, with no penalty. Each success either opens one closed order in a non-Company region or opens China by placing the Superintendent overlay/card; the Chairman immediately hires a writer. After all envoys, the Director may make up to two transfers, each moving one writer or ship between any Presidencies or sea zones, including China once created. The Director cannot transfer while still taking envoys.
answers.evidence: Actions—Director of Trade: Special Envoys and transfer timing.

answers.answer: 1. Military Affairs may make up to two transfers, each moving one officer or regiment from one Army to another while remaining in the top half. Then assign every Officer-in-Training to any Army’s top half. Finally appoint Commanders: if there is a vacancy or someone has more total family pieces in an Army than the current Commander’s family, choose among families with the most pieces. Move the chosen officer to the Commander slot and return the previous Commander to the top as an officer. A tie with the current Commander’s family does not replace them. Nepotism does not apply.
answers.evidence: Actions—Military Affairs: full operation order and replacement rules.

answers.answer: 1. Each President chooses the order of its Commander, Governors and its own Trade, and must allow each position an opportunity to act, though Commander and Governors may decline. Each position finishes all its actions before the next begins; Trade may go before or after a Commander or Governor but cannot interrupt another position. If the President is vacant, the Chairman sets the order only and cannot Trade or approve local alliance purchases.
answers.evidence: Presidency operations and Trade: action order and vacant President rule.

answers.answer: 1. Trade does not exhaust ships. On a nonfinal Refresh, writers on orders return to their associated Presidency’s Writers box, using dividers to preserve affiliation; filled tokens and Presidency dividers return to supply. On the final turn, skip Refresh. Fitted player ships keep fatigue.
answers.evidence: Trade capacity and Upkeep/Refresh table.

answers.answer: 1. At the start of Commander operations, before Deploy attempts, first request the President’s treasury funds for any printed-price local alliances in the Army; the President must approve. Move purchased alliances to the top/active half. When used for Deploy or defense, exhaust the whole alliance to the bottom half. Its strength is usable once that turn and cannot be split among more than one purpose. Refresh exhausts unused active alliances too and does not reactivate them as it does officers and regiments.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy: local alliance purchase, exhaustion and Refresh rules.

answers.answer: 1. For Deploy in an already Company-controlled region to reopen orders or clear unrest, Company defense penalty is zero and no tower remains, so gain zero tower trophies. With no tower or faceup loot modifier, use minimum loot equal to surviving participating officers plus one for the Commander, distributed normally. The Company region still must have unrest or a closed order to give the action an effect; do not take a dead action.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy: target boundary and already-Company-controlled region exception.

answers.answer: 1. Each successful Build performs one stage. If no partial ship is in the Governor’s region, that single success places the partial ship there. If a partial ship is already there, that single success completes it into the sea zone associated with the Governor’s President; the two stages therefore require two successes in total, and the partial ship has no other effect. A commissioned regiment is placed in the Army associated with the Governor’s President; it has officer-like strength, loot is paid to the bank, and it does not roll officer-loss checks.
answers.evidence: Governors—Administer: Build Company ship and Commission regiment options.

answers.answer: 1. China is created by a successful Special Envoy or by the Envoy to China law; in either case the Chairman immediately hires any writer. Its treasury holds ships, not cash. Shipping and Director of Trade may send ships there like any sea zone; China ships count Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws. After Bengal it may act, subject to its single trade attempt.
answers.evidence: Superintendent of Trade in China: creation, hiring, treasury and operating position.

answers.answer: 1. After Bengal, China may attempt Trade only once, including a failed attempt, so there is no retry; roll one die per ship. Without an export icon in Company-controlled regions, do not attempt China Trade. On success, count export icons only in all Company-controlled regions: Company Balance receives £4 times the number of those icons, and the Superintendent’s family receives £1 per icon from the bank. Neither payment counts non-Company export icons, and the Company payment is not a flat £4.
answers.evidence: Superintendent of Trade in China: attempt limits, eligibility and payout table.

answers.answer: 1. When the Governor General law creates the office, immediately make all Governors pensioners, remove their overlays and partially built Company ships, and return Governor/Director cards to the box. Replace Director of Trade with Governor General, preserving holder and fatigue, and place its ribbon overlay. No further Governors or overlays are created upon conquest; printed Company symbols show controlled regions. Governor General hires Presidents and uses former Director’s treasury and turn position; it is hired like Director and rolls attrition normally. Skip Governor Elimination when regions are lost.
answers.evidence: Governor General: law transition and later conquest/loss rules.

answers.answer: 1. First add £3 to Balance per Company region. Then Govern may be attempted repeatedly, paying £1 from its treasury per die with no penalty. Every 6 rolled adds one unrest to each Company region, even on success; failure adds another unrest to every Company region. On success, the Governor General’s family takes £1 from the bank per Company region, then must choose one benefit per region: complete a Company ship into any sea zone including China; place a regiment in any Army; or add £2 to Balance or any office treasury except its own, adding unrest to a Company region. Multiple Tax choices this turn must place their unrest in different regions. At most one successful Govern per turn.
answers.evidence: Governor General: balance bonus, Govern check and success/failure consequences.

answers.answer: 1. A storm die sea-zone result affects that zone; three storms affect all sea zones, and no storm indication means no checks. Company and extra ships are exempt. Check player-owned ships in Company fleets in affected zones; ships assigned to China count Eastern. Firm ships count in the sea zone on their firm strategy even though on a charter; Hobnob firm ships are exempt. Roll once per eligible ship: 1–2 nothing; 3–4 fatigue, or sink if already fatigued; 5–6 sink. Return a sunk ship to its shipyard unfatigued.
answers.evidence: Events—storm result and eligibility table.

answers.answer: 1. When an order newly closes, return any writer on it to its owner’s supply; flip a filled token to closed. If told to close an order in an already fully closed region, Cascade by closing all open orders directly connected to that region’s orders. If a connected order is already closed, close that region’s northernmost open order instead; if none are open, it also Cascades. A region can initiate a Cascade only once per event tile but may receive effects from multiple Cascades.
answers.evidence: Events—Closing orders and Cascades procedure.

answers.answer: 1. Turmoil closes the northernmost open order in the top-stack region; if all are closed, Cascade. Windfall owners take £1 per writer on orders in the top-stack region and every bordering region. Shuffle moves Elephant first, then shuffles that tile with the remaining draw stack; separately shuffle discards and place them on top. If the draw stack is empty, March last instead.
answers.evidence: Events table: Turmoil, Windfall and Shuffle.

answers.answer: 1. Leader gives one tower to the top-stack region if it is sovereign. If it is dominated, it instead rebels with the printed explosion modifier. March only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.
answers.evidence: Events table: Leader procedure.

answers.answer: 1. At a border, Peace opens orders connected across Elephant’s border and adds one tower to each touched non-Company region. If Elephant is wholly inside a region, instead open all its orders and remove its unrest. Then Elephant Marches.
answers.evidence: Events table: Peace procedure.

answers.answer: 1. Invasion Crisis requires the sovereign attacker’s whole empire strength plus event modifier to be greater than the defender’s whole empire strength; equal strength does not win. On success, replace the defender’s flag with the attacker’s dominated flag; taking a capital shatters its entire empire. If the attacker had no empire, use a free capital/star flag and matching small flag; if none are available, no new empire or flags form. On failure, the attacker loses one tower. Sovereign regions have a dome without a flag or a capital/star flag; dominated regions have a small flag or no dome. If an empire loses its last dominated region, remove the surviving capital’s starred flag; this applies regardless of cause.
answers.evidence: Events—India terminology, Invasion Crisis and empire last-region rule.

answers.answer: 1. In Rebellion Crisis, compare only the rebelling region’s strength plus modifier against its sovereign capital’s strength; other regions in the empire do not count. It must be strictly greater, so equal strength does not win. On success the actor becomes sovereign, its flag is removed and all its orders close (Cascade if already closed). On failure, remove one tower from the capital.
answers.evidence: Events—Rebellion Crisis procedure.

answers.answer: 1. On Region Loss, the Commander returns half their family’s trophies rounded up, then the Commander member returns to supply. Roll once per officer in the associated Army; each 6 removes that officer. Eliminate the Governor by returning office card to unused stack, fatigue and member to supplies; remove Governor overlay, partially built Company ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion’s specified strength) and appropriate invasion flag. Return control token to the region with £ loot side down and region-symbol side up; future conquest gets no loot modifier, and the region loses its Presidency association. An Invasion Crisis closes all its orders or Cascades if already closed; Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing loss equals number of regions lost so far this turn, including this one: first −1, second additional −2, etc. If this causes failure, finish Events in India before Final Scoring. Losing one region does not automatically lose another Company region; resolve each other attack and defense separately.
answers.evidence: Events—Region Loss procedure and Company-region cascade note.

answers.answer: 1. After a successful Invasion Crisis, move Elephant to the successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); otherwise move it to the top-stack region. In a Company region place it fully inside. In a dominated region point it toward its sovereign. In a sovereign region point it across the shape-marked border on the tile. If that neighbor is already dominated by the actor, choose the first clockwise neighbor that is not; if all neighbors are dominated, use the redirect-arrow shape’s border pointing toward the empire capital.
answers.evidence: Events—Elephant’s March procedure.

answers.answer: 1. Foreign Invasion rolls the storm die to select targets: West→Bombay, South→Madras, East→Bengal; all storms means each, and none means the top-stack region. For each target, roll an ordinary die for attack strength and resolve Invasion/Company attack. The ordinary attack die is also used to set resulting tower strength at half the roll rounded down; unrest does not add to the primary Foreign Invasion strength or determine tower levels. On success close all target orders, Cascading if they were already all closed; remove target’s flag and all matching flags if it is a capital, restore dome if Company-controlled, and set tower strength to half the attack roll rounded down. March with circle shape only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that was invaded.
answers.evidence: Events—Foreign Invasion row and FAQ designer ruling.

answers.answer: 1. The PM must draw at least one law, revealing them one at a time. After one or two ordinary non-dilemma draws, the PM may stop or continue to at most three total, then chooses any one revealed law and discards the others. Drawing a dilemma forces selection of that dilemma and immediately ends drawing. Before voting, the PM moves the dial arm clockwise or counterclockwise, stopping at the first policy space matching the chosen law’s bottom icon; that space fixes the target and consequence.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets: law drawing and policy selection.

answers.answer: 1. Tax: each family pays £1 to the bank per target it owns; each unpaid target returns to supply, including a taxed Chairman. A fitted ship belonging to a lost shipyard stays in play, and the shipyard cannot be bought until the ship returns; losing a prize or luxury removes its VP. Window tax additionally requires payment for each window on enterprises and each family member’s prize when the selected policy includes windows; return the enterprise or prize member if unable. Bonus: the bank pays each family £1 per target it owns. Power: swap the target Power marker with the next higher marker; if it is already highest, swap any other pair.
answers.evidence: Parliament policy table: Tax, Window tax, Bonus and Power.

answers.answer: 1. Starting with PM and proceeding clockwise, players cast votes; each £1 of family cash buys one vote, plus printed card votes. Each card’s votes may be used only once in the entire vote, across all rounds: rotate it when used and leave it rotated until resolution, so it cannot vote again in a later round of that vote. Adjust support up or down; tracks are unlimited. PM may call another full round or stop after each round; a round with no votes must end voting.
answers.evidence: Parliament—Voting procedure.

answers.answer: 1. A player who voted for may later oppose; once opposed, they cannot vote for during that vote. Track all opposition votes: the biggest opponent holds Opposition Leader, and a tied current holder retains it. With the recipient’s consent, votes may be cast for someone who already opposed or commits to oppose, and are added to that person’s opposition total. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except when forced to use the “Vote with my enterprises” promise.
answers.evidence: Parliament—Voting: opposition, leader, coalition and PM exception.

answers.answer: 1. Yes. Pay printed upkeep separately for each family member on a prize, including on the final turn. If unpaid, return that member and lose that prize’s printed VP. On a final turn perform upkeep but skip Refresh and go to Final Scoring. On nonfinal turns, return writers on orders to their associated Presidency’s Writers box using dividers to preserve affiliation; return filled tokens and dividers to supply; return extra ships to supply; reactivate exhausted Army officers and regiments; exhaust active local alliances without reactivating them; fitted player ships keep fatigue; then advance one turn and begin London Season.
answers.evidence: Upkeep and Refresh procedure/table.

answers.answer: 1. Each shareholder may make one additional retirement per London Season from supply rather than Pensioners, regardless of how many firms they own. Actual cash spent after spouse discounts cannot exceed the highest total dividend marker of any firm where they own a share; printed prize cost may exceed the marker if discounts cover the difference. No retirement from a firm whose marker is absent or zero. Spouse discounts can allow a higher printed-cost prize; retirement otherwise follows normal rules, including prestige eligibility. At the start of Final Scoring, score firms then permit one special retirement regardless of Company success or failure, before normal final-scoring steps; no display cards in Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: Deregulation—Special retirement paragraph and Final Scoring order.

answers.answer: 1. A firm has London and India treasuries. London receives the bank’s £5 per investment and pays for ship acquisition, trade bids and expenses; India receives trade proceeds and pays dividends/expenses. Investment cash always comes from the bank to London. London cash cannot buy new equity shares; creating shares requires a Company-share or workshop contribution. Family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries; only specified investment, payout and expense procedures move money. Dividends are paid from India treasury only.
answers.evidence: Deregulation—firm treasuries paragraph and firm dividend procedure.

answers.answer: 1. After Family share creation and before Hiring, the Firms investment phase proceeds without set order until nobody wants more actions. The manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm; the PM resolves conflicts between firms. Then managers choose strategies.
answers.evidence: Firms phase: investments timing paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. A firm may fit a ship from its own or another player’s shipyard only with that shipyard owner’s consent, paying £3 from the firm’s London treasury to the bank. It may buy a player-owned ship already in Company only with that owner’s consent: pay £3 for an unfatigued ship or £2 for a fatigued ship into Shipping treasury. Firms cannot acquire Company ships or extra ships.
answers.evidence: Firms phase—Ships rule.

answers.answer: 1. Only a player who manages no firm at all may initiate a hostile takeover; managing a different firm also makes them ineligible. Obtain consent from holders of a majority of the target firm’s shares, then move its ships, money and shares to the new charter and copy both cube positions. The former manager returns cubes and flips their board to the family side.
answers.evidence: Firms phase—Hostile takeover procedure.

answers.answer: 1. Managers negotiate a merger with every shareholder’s consent. The highest-value firm is primary; if tied, players choose among the tied firms. Transfer all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to the primary, and return secondary boards to family sides; players may negotiate share transfers. If the primary would exceed ten shares, return excess shares to their owners’ supplies with those owners’ consent. The entire agreement is one binding immediate transfer, and the primary’s value/dividend track remains the continuing firm’s track.
answers.evidence: Firms phase—Merger procedure and ten-share limit.

answers.answer: 1. A firm selects exactly one trade attempt per turn; only a firm with at least one ship may select a trade strategy. Hobnob has no bid, trade or dividends, but the firm still pays expenses and retains its previous dividend marker for retirement. Hobnob firm ships are exempt from storms.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies table and storm exposure table.

answers.answer: 1. Yes. Emergency investments follow normal Company-share/workshop rules, even when the ten-share cap prevents creating more shares: pay expenses, lose any remaining cash and lower Value one space per emergency investment. The same-turn share restriction remains part of the normal contribution rules: cannot use shares created this turn, even after trading them away; Chairman shares cannot be used, and Company shares cannot be used when Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space. A contribution is a Company share or workshop; the summary does not say firm value itself is an investment resource.
answers.evidence: Investment restrictions and emergency investments procedure.

answers.answer: 1. An emergency negotiated merger may involve only one other firm. The normal merger procedure still applies, including every involved shareholder’s consent. The other firm must first pay its own expenses if not already paid, then cover the endangered firm’s unpaid expenses.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: emergency merger rule.

answers.answer: 1. Voluntary dissolution requires consent of all shareholders. Apply the same procedure as for an insolvent firm: shares go to Debtor’s Prison (each −1 VP), ships return to their matching shipyards, and the charter flips to its family side. Workshops remain invested for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Firms phase—Voluntary dissolution and insolvency dissolution procedures.

answers.answer: 1. Before ordinary Power, Court or final-outcome scoring, each player adds VP from all shares across all their firms and rounds that player’s total down once, then deducts 1 VP per their family piece in Debtor’s Prison. Firm Value per-share VP is: Value 1 = −1; 2 = 0; 3–4 = ½; 5–7 = 1; 8–9 = 1½; 10 = 2. Next comes one special firm retirement per eligible shareholder, then ordinary Power/Court/outcome scoring. Company survival/failure does not change firm scoring; on Company failure, separately subtract Court’s current VP per Company share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop, while invested workshops do not score that VP.
answers.evidence: Final Scoring order, firm VP/value table and Court/workshops rule.

answers.answer: 1. Prize values per family member are: cost £2, upkeep £0, 0 VP, 0 windows; cost £4, upkeep £1, 2 VP, 1 window; cost £8, upkeep £2, 4 VP, 2 windows; cost £14, upkeep £3, 8 VP, 3 windows; cost £20, upkeep £4, 12 VP, 4 windows.
answers.evidence: Prizes table.

answers.answer: 1. 1710 runs turns 1–5, starts at £10 expectations and Debt 0, with Royal Protection; it has no deregulation procedures. 1758 runs turns 3–7 and starts with the Company monopoly; deregulation can be voted in. Long 1710 runs turns 1–8, same initial position as 1710, with deregulation available separately. 1813 runs turns 5–8 and starts deregulated, allowing firms.
answers.evidence: Scenario overview and scenario figures table.

answers.answer: 1. 1710: turns 1–5; initial Standing expectations £10 and Debt 0; each office treasury £3; Royal Protection; one regiment per Army and no Company ships. 1758: turns 3–7; initial Standing expectations £12 and Debt 3; each office treasury £4; Calico Acts; one regiment per Army and one Company ship in East Indian. Place the Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency.
answers.evidence: Scenario figures table and corrected setup token note.

answers.answer: 1. For 1813, use turns 5–8, Standing expectations £10 and Debt 0, £3 in each office treasury, Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor’s Prison side) and Calico Acts, two regiments per Army and one Company ship per sea zone. Put the +2/−2 share-value token in Court, create China, and place Bombay, Madras and Bengal control tokens in their Presidencies. Return Governor General law to the box and place its office overlay over Director of Trade; use Governor General instead of Director and use no Governors. Copy India towers, flags, closed orders and Elephant from the scenario card reverse. Starting player-owned ships and offices also come from dealt setup cards.
answers.evidence: Scenario figures and 1813 setup paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. Power awards are 3 VP for most and 1 VP for second on final turns 1–3; 5/2 VP on turns 4–6; and 8/4 VP on turns 7–8. A tied-first group gets only the lower award each, with no other award; tied second receive none.
answers.evidence: Power award paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. Initial Power positions: Social at 2, Company shares at 1, Shipping and Manufacturing at 0. Standing expectations run £4/£6/£8/£10/£12/£14/£16, and reset S is above £10. Lined Standing £4/£6/£8 or Debt 5/6/7/8 permits the PM to call the special Deregulation vote; starred Standing £4 or Debt 8 requires the PM to call it.
answers.evidence: Start Power positions and Deregulation thresholds paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. The ruling says unrest does not add to a Foreign Invasion’s primary attack strength or determine its resulting tower levels. Use the ordinary die roll for both attack strength and halving to create towers; do not apply normal primary Crisis added unrest. On a successful Foreign Invasion, close all target orders once; if already all closed, Cascade instead. Region Loss does not close them a second time; its added closure applies only to a normal Invasion Crisis.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Foreign Invasion and unrest (designer clarification).

answers.answer: 1. If Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reduces a check to zero dice, it means failure. Company Fraud is played at start of Revenue: roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Balance by twice the highest roll (minimum zero), and take cash from the bank equal to the actual Balance reduction. Public Demands Impeachment returns the member to supply and the office card to vacancies. Military Oversight demotes one Commander to an officer, then appoints a Commander from officers; the same former Commander remains eligible to become Commander again. These are card-specific effects, not changes to normal check/hiring procedures.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Applicable official errata, card-specific corrections.

answers.answer: 1. For shared setup, set Company Balance to £5, put family VP markers at zero, put local alliances in their named Army boxes, and put loot tokens money-side up in matching regions. Choose a scenario and follow its card for Standing, Debt, treasuries, laws, regiments, ships and India political map. Put Turn marker on the scenario’s date and point PM dial arm to the matching date; scenario determines final turn.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–2.

answers.answer: 1. The turn order is London Season → Family → Firms (if deregulated) → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh. The Firms phase is after Family and before Hiring. On the game’s first turn, skip London Season. An eligible special Deregulation vote occurs at the very start of the turn, before London Season.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. Retirements start with the Chairman, or former Chairman if the office is vacant, then proceed clockwise. Each player may retire each pensioner to a prize: pay its printed cost, move member to the prize and gain printed VP. Set actual spending aside until London Season ends to establish display-selection order, then pay the bank. Pensioners not retired do not remain for another turn; remaining Pensioners return to supplies after the display step.
answers.evidence: London Season—Retirements and Prestige.

answers.answer: 1. Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region, remove the surviving capital’s starred flag: it is no longer an empire. This applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest of that last dominated region.
answers.evidence: India terminology: last dominated region rule.

answers.answer: 1. Firm Value 1 earns −1 VP per share; Value 2 earns 0; Values 3–4 earn ½; Values 5–7 earn 1; Values 8–9 earn 1½; and Value 10 earns 2 VP per share.
answers.evidence: Firm-track VP per share table.

answers.answer: 1. Starting with the Chairman title holder, clockwise, each player resolves their family action. After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one; repeat while both remain. With no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order.
answers.evidence: Family phase order and New Company shares procedure.

answers.answer: 1. Follow the red ribbon left to right: Chairman → Director of Trade (or Governor General) → Manager of Shipping → Military Affairs → Bombay Presidency → Madras Presidency → Bengal Presidency → China Superintendent, if created. Skip each vacant office. Within each Presidency, its President chooses the order of Commander, Governor(s) and Trade; each position finishes before the next acts. Each office spends only its own treasury. Offices created by actions go into Vacant Offices unless immediate hiring is specified; a newly created Governorship normally waits until a later Hiring phase. China acts after Bengal.
answers.evidence: Company Operation and Presidency sequence paragraphs.

answers.answer: 1. First roll the storm die: a sea-zone result affects that zone, three storms affect all sea zones, and no storm indication means no storm checks. Company and extra ships are exempt; player-owned ships in Company fleets in affected zones are checked; ships assigned to China count Eastern; firm ships count in the sea zone on their firm strategy; Hobnob firm ships are exempt. Roll once per eligible ship: 1–2 nothing; 3–4 fatigue, or sink if already fatigued; 5–6 sink, and return a sunk ship to its shipyard unfatigued. The die face also gives the number of India events. Resolve all required storms before drawing any event. Then flip and resolve one tile at a time from the draw stack, for as many events as the number printed on the die face. Where an event uses a region, normally read the back of the new top tile in the draw stack, not the tile just drawn, and follow each event’s specific location rule.
answers.evidence: Events in India: storm, event count/order and location rules.

answers.answer: 1. The Elephant’s tail is the attacker/acting region and its head is the defender. A sovereign actor causes Invasion; a dominated actor causes Rebellion against its sovereign; if Elephant is wholly inside a Company region, resolve Rebellion against the Company. Sovereign regions have a dome without a flag or a capital/star flag; dominated regions have a small flag or no dome. Tower levels show region strength and the dome adds none.
answers.evidence: India terminology and ordinary Crisis classifier.
